# Pea protein

<section class="hmi-quick-read" id="pea-protein-quick-read" data-hmi-quick-read aria-labelledby="pea-protein-quick-read-label"><div class="hmi-quick-read-label" id="pea-protein-quick-read-label">Quick read</div>

Pea protein in the HMI library has 18 reported results for lead, cadmium, total mercury, nickel, chromium and tin from 2 sources.<sup class="cite">[[sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ring G, Sheehan A, Lehane M, Furey A · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Development, Validation and Application of an ICP-SFMS Method for the Determination of Metals in Protein Powder Samples, Sourced in Ireland, with Risk Assessment for Irish Consumers</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Molecules, 26, 4347</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/lopezcalabozo2025-vegetable-protein-concentrates|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Rocio Lopez-Calabozo, Ivan Martinez-Martin, Marta Rodriguez-Fernandez, Yamina Absi, Ana Maria Vivar-Quintana, Isabel Revilla · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/lopezcalabozo2025-vegetable-protein-concentrates">The Influence of the Nutritional and Mineral Composition of Vegetable Protein Concentrates on Their Functional Properties</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/lopezcalabozo2025-vegetable-protein-concentrates">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

<ul>
<li>
<strong>Metals measured:</strong>

Lead, cadmium, total mercury, nickel, chromium and tin, in 18 results from 2 sources.<sup class="cite">[[sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ring G, Sheehan A, Lehane M, Furey A · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Development, Validation and Application of an ICP-SFMS Method for the Determination of Metals in Protein Powder Samples, Sourced in Ireland, with Risk Assessment for Irish Consumers</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Molecules, 26, 4347</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/lopezcalabozo2025-vegetable-protein-concentrates|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Rocio Lopez-Calabozo, Ivan Martinez-Martin, Marta Rodriguez-Fernandez, Yamina Absi, Ana Maria Vivar-Quintana, Isabel Revilla · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/lopezcalabozo2025-vegetable-protein-concentrates">The Influence of the Nutritional and Mineral Composition of Vegetable Protein Concentrates on Their Functional Properties</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/lopezcalabozo2025-vegetable-protein-concentrates">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</li>
<li>
<strong>Main drivers:</strong>

Form, basis and where the pea protein was sampled; reporting limits decide how many results are non-detects.<sup class="cite">[[sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ring G, Sheehan A, Lehane M, Furey A · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Development, Validation and Application of an ICP-SFMS Method for the Determination of Metals in Protein Powder Samples, Sourced in Ireland, with Risk Assessment for Irish Consumers</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Molecules, 26, 4347</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/lopezcalabozo2025-vegetable-protein-concentrates|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Rocio Lopez-Calabozo, Ivan Martinez-Martin, Marta Rodriguez-Fernandez, Yamina Absi, Ana Maria Vivar-Quintana, Isabel Revilla · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/lopezcalabozo2025-vegetable-protein-concentrates">The Influence of the Nutritional and Mineral Composition of Vegetable Protein Concentrates on Their Functional Properties</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/lopezcalabozo2025-vegetable-protein-concentrates">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</li>
<li>
<strong>Practical framing:</strong>

The EU sets a maximum of 100 µg/kg cadmium for proteins from pulses (as set for that ingredient row).<sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 of 25 April of 2023 on maximum levels for certain contaminants in food and repealing Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</li>
</ul>
</section>

<a id="pea-protein-overview"></a>
<a id="decision-summary"></a>
## Pea protein overview

<a id="hmi-ing-004"></a>
<a id="which-contamination-concerns-are-supported-for-this-ingredient-and-its-defined-forms"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-005"></a>
<a id="which-sourcing-or-production-decisions-deserve-priority-on-the-available-evidence"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-006"></a>
<a id="which-evidence-gaps-most-limit-those-decisions"></a>

Pea protein in the HMI library has 18 reported results for lead, cadmium, total mercury, nickel, chromium and tin from 2 sources.<sup class="cite">[[sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ring G, Sheehan A, Lehane M, Furey A · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Development, Validation and Application of an ICP-SFMS Method for the Determination of Metals in Protein Powder Samples, Sourced in Ireland, with Risk Assessment for Irish Consumers</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Molecules, 26, 4347</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/lopezcalabozo2025-vegetable-protein-concentrates|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Rocio Lopez-Calabozo, Ivan Martinez-Martin, Marta Rodriguez-Fernandez, Yamina Absi, Ana Maria Vivar-Quintana, Isabel Revilla · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/lopezcalabozo2025-vegetable-protein-concentrates">The Influence of the Nutritional and Mineral Composition of Vegetable Protein Concentrates on Their Functional Properties</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/lopezcalabozo2025-vegetable-protein-concentrates">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>



For a buyer the practical points are the form bought, the basis a result is reported on, where the pea protein came from and the laboratory’s reporting limit. The EU sets a maximum of 100 µg/kg cadmium for proteins from pulses (as set for that ingredient row).<sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 of 25 April of 2023 on maximum levels for certain contaminants in food and repealing Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Testing finds contamination but does not remove it.



<a id="ingredient-identity-and-scope"></a>
## What counts as pea protein

<a id="hmi-ing-001"></a>
<a id="what-commodity-biological-species-edible-part-and-commercial-forms-does-this-page-cover"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-002"></a>
<a id="which-processing-states-and-derivatives-are-distinct-materials-rather-than-synonyms"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-003"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-can-be-transferred-between-those-materials-and-what-requires-a-separate-answer"></a>

This page covers pea protein in 2 forms kept separate in every comparison: pea protein, powder or ground (10 results) and pea protein, as sold (8 results).<sup class="cite">[[sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ring G, Sheehan A, Lehane M, Furey A · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Development, Validation and Application of an ICP-SFMS Method for the Determination of Metals in Protein Powder Samples, Sourced in Ireland, with Risk Assessment for Irish Consumers</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Molecules, 26, 4347</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/lopezcalabozo2025-vegetable-protein-concentrates|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Rocio Lopez-Calabozo, Ivan Martinez-Martin, Marta Rodriguez-Fernandez, Yamina Absi, Ana Maria Vivar-Quintana, Isabel Revilla · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/lopezcalabozo2025-vegetable-protein-concentrates">The Influence of the Nutritional and Mineral Composition of Vegetable Protein Concentrates on Their Functional Properties</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/lopezcalabozo2025-vegetable-protein-concentrates">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Results stay on the basis each source reports: as sold or fresh weight, dry weight, or unstated. Dry-weight, as-sold and unstated results are never pooled, and no moisture conversion is applied.

## Heavy metal contamination profile of pea protein

<a id="hmi-ing-007"></a>
<a id="which-metals-and-chemical-species-have-been-investigated-in-this-ingredient"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-008"></a>
<a id="what-concentrations-detection-frequencies-and-variability-were-observed-in-each-defined-sampling-frame"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-009"></a>
<a id="which-analyte-questions-are-unassessed-access-blocked-conflicting-or-searched-without-eligible-evidence"></a>

The table holds every extracted pea protein result: one row for each statistic a source reports for a form, group and metal, 18 rows in all, grouped by metal and form; percentiles, ranges and maxima for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row.<sup class="cite">[[sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ring G, Sheehan A, Lehane M, Furey A · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Development, Validation and Application of an ICP-SFMS Method for the Determination of Metals in Protein Powder Samples, Sourced in Ireland, with Risk Assessment for Irish Consumers</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Molecules, 26, 4347</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/lopezcalabozo2025-vegetable-protein-concentrates|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Rocio Lopez-Calabozo, Ivan Martinez-Martin, Marta Rodriguez-Fernandez, Yamina Absi, Ana Maria Vivar-Quintana, Isabel Revilla · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/lopezcalabozo2025-vegetable-protein-concentrates">The Influence of the Nutritional and Mineral Composition of Vegetable Protein Concentrates on Their Functional Properties</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/lopezcalabozo2025-vegetable-protein-concentrates">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Monitoring medians are HMI calculations from individual submissions; non-detects remain intervals between zero and the reporting limit and are never read as zero.

0 rows can be rated against an HMI reference for the same form and basis, 0 rows have a direct same-study comparison, and the rest stay unrated with the reason recorded.

<div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-pea-protein" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-pea-protein-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of pea protein, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

<a id="processing-cooking-and-preparation"></a>
<a id="processing-effects-and-derivatives"></a>
## Processing, cooking and preparation

<a id="hmi-ing-016"></a>
<a id="how-do-specified-processing-or-preparation-steps-change-the-measured-metal-endpoints"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-017"></a>
<a id="how-do-derivatives-concentrates-extracts-and-fractions-differ-from-their-parent-ingredient"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-018"></a>
<a id="do-changes-reflect-removal-redistribution-moisture-or-yield-change-dilution-or-altered-species-or-availability"></a>

No study in the library measured the same pea protein before and after washing, peeling, drying or cooking for metals, so no processing effect can be stated. Heat does not destroy metals; cooking or drying changes a concentration by moving water or metal, not by removing the element.


<a id="mitigation-for-pea-protein"></a>
<a id="mitigation-options"></a>
## Mitigation for pea protein

<a id="hmi-ing-019"></a>
<a id="which-prevention-mitigation-or-remediation-measures-have-been-evaluated-for-this-ingredient"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-020"></a>
<a id="under-what-conditions-at-which-stage-and-against-which-comparator-do-they-work-or-fail"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-021"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-supports-field-or-commercial-implementation-and-ongoing-verification"></a>

No control for metals in pea protein was measured in the library; lot testing against the applicable limit remains the verifiable step.

<p class="hmi-mitigation-gap" data-mitigation-gap>No study in this library has yet measured a way to lower heavy metals in pea protein; the results above show the levels measured, and lot testing against the applicable limit remains the verifiable check.</p>



<a id="trade-offs-and-failure-modes"></a>
## Trade-offs and limits of controls

<a id="hmi-ing-022"></a>
<a id="can-an-intervention-increase-another-contaminant-or-redistribute-contamination-to-a-by-product"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-023"></a>

<a id="hmi-ing-024"></a>
<a id="what-costs-constraints-adverse-effects-or-failure-modes-are-documented-and-which-are-unknown"></a>

Metals do not move together, so a lot that passes a lead limit says little about cadmium, arsenic or nickel unless those are tested as well.

<a id="what-can-a-certificate-of-analysis-or-non-detect-establish-and-what-remains-untested"></a>

Results depend on the method and its reporting limit. Reporting limits for lead were 0.026 µg/kg where sources stated them.<sup class="cite">[[sources/lopezcalabozo2025-vegetable-protein-concentrates|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Rocio Lopez-Calabozo, Ivan Martinez-Martin, Marta Rodriguez-Fernandez, Yamina Absi, Ana Maria Vivar-Quintana, Isabel Revilla · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/lopezcalabozo2025-vegetable-protein-concentrates">The Influence of the Nutritional and Mineral Composition of Vegetable Protein Concentrates on Their Functional Properties</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/lopezcalabozo2025-vegetable-protein-concentrates">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Reporting limits for cadmium were 0.015 µg/kg where sources stated them.<sup class="cite">[[sources/lopezcalabozo2025-vegetable-protein-concentrates|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Rocio Lopez-Calabozo, Ivan Martinez-Martin, Marta Rodriguez-Fernandez, Yamina Absi, Ana Maria Vivar-Quintana, Isabel Revilla · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/lopezcalabozo2025-vegetable-protein-concentrates">The Influence of the Nutritional and Mineral Composition of Vegetable Protein Concentrates on Their Functional Properties</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/lopezcalabozo2025-vegetable-protein-concentrates">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

A useful lot result names the form, the basis and a quantification limit well below the limit that applies.<sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 of 25 April of 2023 on maximum levels for certain contaminants in food and repealing Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

<a id="universal-faqs"></a>
## Pea protein FAQs

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-pea-protein" data-anchor="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-pea-protein" data-question="What heavy metals are found in pea protein?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What heavy metals are found in pea protein?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

The library reports lead, cadmium, total mercury, nickel, chromium and tin in pea protein, most often lead, cadmium and total mercury.<sup class="cite">[[sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ring G, Sheehan A, Lehane M, Furey A · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Development, Validation and Application of an ICP-SFMS Method for the Determination of Metals in Protein Powder Samples, Sourced in Ireland, with Risk Assessment for Irish Consumers</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Molecules, 26, 4347</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/lopezcalabozo2025-vegetable-protein-concentrates|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Rocio Lopez-Calabozo, Ivan Martinez-Martin, Marta Rodriguez-Fernandez, Yamina Absi, Ana Maria Vivar-Quintana, Isabel Revilla · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/lopezcalabozo2025-vegetable-protein-concentrates">The Influence of the Nutritional and Mineral Composition of Vegetable Protein Concentrates on Their Functional Properties</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/lopezcalabozo2025-vegetable-protein-concentrates">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="are-there-legal-limits-for-heavy-metals-in-pea-protein" data-anchor="are-there-legal-limits-for-heavy-metals-in-pea-protein" data-question="Are there legal limits for heavy metals in pea protein?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Are there legal limits for heavy metals in pea protein?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

The EU sets a maximum of 100 µg/kg cadmium for proteins from pulses (as set for that ingredient row).<sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 of 25 April of 2023 on maximum levels for certain contaminants in food and repealing Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> It sets 1,000 µg/kg cadmium for food supplements (as placed on the market, when the product is sold as a food supplement).<sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 of 25 April of 2023 on maximum levels for certain contaminants in food and repealing Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

## What remains uncertain

Arsenic and inorganic arsenic were not measured in these pea protein rows. Mercury was measured in two Irish retail powders and not in the concentrate study. Cadmium and lead non-detects in the concentrates use detection limits printed under the ppb heading; the footnotes do not restate the unit. Two quantified retail powders are not enough for a rated reference. Growing origin is not reported. No study here measured a before-and-after reduction of metals in pea protein.
